title: One Post, Two Time Zones: 10 AM Everywhere | vitalii.no
description:
My platform targets New York and Oslo. Publishing new features at a single UTC time meant one audience always caught it at an inconvenient hour — a 10 AM UTC post landed at 6 AM in New York and noon in Oslo. Visibility and engagement suffered, and hard work felt wasted on half the audience.

I built a timezone-aware scheduler orchestrated by an hourly GitHub Action. A TypeScript script queries Supabase's scheduled_posts table filtered by locale and scheduled_at_utc, calculates each locale's target 10 AM local time — America/New_York, Europe/Oslo — converts it to UTC, and checks whether the current time falls within a 15-minute window. On a match it invokes the publish_feature_post Supabase Edge Function, which flips the post to published.

Posts now land at 10 AM local time for every audience, and the payoff showed up immediately: an estimated 20 to 30% lift in click-through rate and shares within the first hour of publishing.
